title: Fake news, Covid-19 e Infodemia: un esempio di ricerca sociale in real-time su Twitter
screen_reason: Big-data analysis of 7,237,581 Italian-language Covid-19 tweets (20 Feb - 2 May 2020). The paper reports the share of tweets in that corpus that carry fake news: 1.44% (104,221) by keyword-matching to ten Ministry-of-Health-listed false claims, and 75 tweets carrying URLs from the Bufale.net / Butac.it fake-news domain blacklist. Both are shares of items in a sample judged against an external ground truth, with a stated denominator, i.e. CONTENT prevalence estimates. Text is Italian; quotes are given verbatim with English translations in the notes.

estimates.measure_type: % of Italian Covid-19 tweets containing at least one keyword of the ten most popular Covid-19 fake news (Ministry of Health debunk list)
estimates.denominator: 7,237,581 Italian-language tweets collected from the Twitter Streaming API with 21 Covid-19 keywords/hashtags between 20/02/2020 and 02/05/2020 (posted by 22,577 unique users)
estimates.definition: Tweet whose text contains at least one of the ten search queries operationalising the ten most popular Covid-19 fake news listed by the Italian Ministry of Health (colloidal silver cures it; bioterrorism weapon; vitamin C cures it; Montagnier says it is artificial; caused by 5G; Panzironi method cures it; a Soros plan; Avigan cures it; a Gates plan; Africans are immune/irresponsible/contagious)
estimates.misinfo_def: 'Le fake news sono definibili come informazioni fittizie che, da una parte cercano di imitare i contenuti dei news media mainstream ... ma dall'altra ne ignorano, in maniera piu o meno deliberata, le prassi e le norme editoriali' (Lazer et al. 2018)
estimates.source_quote: Su un totale di 7.237.581 tweet, l'1,44% (104.221) contiene almeno una delle keyword che rimandano alle 10 fake news elencate sopra. Di questi il 34% consiste in messaggi anti fake news.
estimates.page_loc: Section 'Fake news: analisi dei link e delle keyword', p. 178; also Abstract and Discussione p. 180
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The ten claims counted as fake news are taken from the Italian Ministry of Health's official Covid-19 debunking page ('Covid-19 - Attenti alle bufale', Ministero della Salute 2020); the authors turned each into a text query and matched tweets automatically with a purpose-written Python script. A separate machine-learning classifier then split pro- vs anti-fake-news tweets, but no accuracy or reliability statistics are reported for either step.
estimates.moderator_quote: Nel nostro caso abbiamo usato le seguenti keyword per raccogliere tweet in lingua italiana: #coronavirus, #covid19, #covid-19, #iorestoacasa, ... Al fine dell'analisi discussa in questo contributo abbiamo estratto dal server un dataset di 7.237.581 tweet, che copre un arco temporale che va da dal 20/02/2020 al 02/05/2020.
estimates.notes: ENGLISH TRANSLATION of source_quote: 'Out of a total of 7,237,581 tweets, 1.44% (104,221) contain at least one of the keywords referring to the 10 fake news listed above. Of these, 34% are anti-fake-news messages.' The abstract states it as 'Only 1,44% of the tweets collected are fake news'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT (why borderline=true): the numerator is tweets MENTIONING a false claim, and the authors themselves report that 34% of them are debunking/anti-fake-news messages; a 'pro-fake-news only' figure would be a computed complement and is forbidden by R8, so the paper's own headline 1.44% is kept, with this caveat recorded. Denominator is every tweet in the topical corpus (items that exist) -> CONTENT, not SHARING: the corpus is all captured tweets, not a set of reshares. ground_truth=fact_checker because the falsity list is an official Ministry of Health debunk list; the item-level matching itself is automated keyword search (arguably 'classifier'), which is noted in ground_truth_detail.

estimates.measure_type: % of Italian Covid-19 tweets containing a URL to a blacklisted fake-news website
estimates.value_raw: 75 of 7,237,581 tweets ('Su 7.237.581 tweet raccolti, solo 75 contengono Url che rimandano a fake news') = 0.001%
estimates.denominator: 7,237,581 Italian-language Covid-19 tweets (containing 1,103,184 URLs in total)
estimates.definition: Tweet containing a URL matching a list of fake-news websites built from the blacklists published by Bufale.net and Butac.it; only three such domains appeared at all (Sputniknews, Imolaoggi, BlastingNews)
estimates.misinfo_def: Same Lazer et al. / Wardle & Derakhshan framing; operationalised here as content published by a blacklisted fake-news outlet
estimates.source_quote: Su 7.237.581 tweet raccolti, solo 75 contengono Url che rimandano a fake news, mentre un residuale 1,44 % tratta di argomenti legati a notizie false nel corpo del testo.
estimates.page_loc: Discussione, p. 180 (see also 'Fake news: analisi dei link e delle keyword', p. 178)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: A Python script extracted every URL in the corpus and matched it against a fake-news domain list compiled from Bufale.net and Butac.it. No inter-coder or validation statistics apply; the list's construction is described only as 'gli elenchi di siti di fake news disponibili su Bufale.net e Butac.it'.
estimates.moderator_quote: Su 1.103.184 Url presenti nei tweet contenuti nel nostro dataset, solo 3 rimandano a siti collocati in "lista nera" da Bufale.net o Butac.it: questi sono Sputniknews ..., Imolaoggi ... e BlastingNews ... Nessuno di questi indirizzi compare piu di 75 volte nei tweet presenti nel dataset.
estimates.notes: ENGLISH TRANSLATION of source_quote: 'Of the 7,237,581 tweets collected, only 75 contain URLs pointing to fake news, while a residual 1.44% deals with topics related to false news in the body of the text.' English translation of moderator_quote: 'Of the 1,103,184 URLs present in the tweets in our dataset, only 3 point to sites blacklisted by Bufale.net or Butac.it ... None of these addresses appears more than 75 times in the tweets in the dataset.' The 0.001% is an exact part/whole share from two verbatim counts in the SAME sentence with the same denominator (75 / 7,237,581), which R8 permits. ADJUDICATOR NOTE: the paper is internally inconsistent about the 75 - Methods says no blacklisted domain appears MORE THAN 75 times (an upper bound per domain, so the true total could be up to ~225 tweets), while the Discussion says exactly 75 tweets contain such URLs. The Discussion wording is used because it names the denominator explicitly; the ambiguity is why confidence is medium. This is the domain-list variant of the same corpus, hence definition_variant=true; breadth is blank because classification is source-level.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) '61% of fake news deals with the topic of immigration' (and, within that category, 77% pro-fake-news) is a TOPIC composition inside the 104,221-tweet misinformation subset, not a falsity share of a general denominator, so it is not a prevalence estimate; not extracted. (2) '34% consists of anti-fake-news messages' is likewise a composition within the misinformation subset; the complement (66% pro) would be a computed complement, forbidden by R8, so no row. (3) Table 3 (top-10 most retweeted accounts inside the fake-news subset, e.g. RadioSavana with 52,946 retweets received) and Table 2 (top-10 accounts by fake news posted, max 191) are bare counts of accounts and retweets: no conc_group_pct / conc_share_pct pair is stated anywhere, so R1 fails and NO CONCENTRATION row can be built, even though the paper's qualitative claim is that fake news circulates in small closed far-right communities. (4) 22,577 unique users, mean 13.7 tweets each (median 2), 1.9 retweets and 1.9 mentions on average are activity descriptives, not misinformation shares. (5) No survey, exposure-log, reach or self-report measure exists in this paper.

rob.design: Real-time big-data digital-methods study, no sampling of humans. Frame: Twitter Streaming API queried from 20/02/2020 with 21 Italian Covid-19 keywords/hashtags (the keyword set was updated during collection as new trending hashtags and political events appeared, which the authors flag as a limitation); the analysed extract runs 20/02/2020-02/05/2020 and contains 7,237,581 tweets from 22,577 unique users. Misinformation identified two ways: (a) URL matching against a fake-news domain list built from Bufale.net and Butac.it; (b) text matching against ten queries operationalising the ten most popular Covid-19 fake news listed by the Italian Ministry of Health, plus a bespoke machine-learning classifier separating pro- from anti-fake-news tweets. NO reliability, precision/recall or validation statistics are reported for the keyword matching or the classifier, and no human coding was performed. Retweet-network analysis used centrality indices. Authors' own limitations: possible missed keywords, Twitter may be the wrong platform (fake news migrating to closed Facebook/Telegram groups and Twitter's own labelling/removal during the pandemic), and the ambiguity of operationalising 'fake news'.
rob.item6_quote: Le fake news sono definibili come informazioni fittizie che, da una parte cercano di imitare i contenuti dei news media mainstream (in termini di format e stile narrativo), ma dall'altra ne ignorano, in maniera piu o meno deliberata, le prassi e le norme editoriali (ad esempio, in termini di deontologia, accuratezza delle fonti, credibilita dell'informazione) (Lazer et al 2018). [EN: 'Fake news can be defined as fictitious information that on the one hand tries to imitate the content of mainstream news media (in format and narrative style) but on the other more or less deliberately ignores their editorial practices and norms (e.g. ethics, source accuracy, credibility of information).']
rob.item10_quote: Su un totale di 7.237.581 tweet, l'1,44% (104.221) contiene almeno una delle keyword che rimandano alle 10 fake news elencate sopra. [EN: 'Out of a total of 7,237,581 tweets, 1.44% (104,221) contain at least one of the keywords referring to the 10 fake news listed above.']
